destination.name: Beowa National Park
destination.tagline: Far South Coast park of whale-watching headlands, beaches and the Light to Light walk.
destination.description: Beowa National Park, formerly Ben Boyd National Park, spans 47 km of rocky coastline near Eden and was renamed in 2022; beowa means "orca" in the language of the Thaua people. It is split by Twofold Bay into the Pambula-Haycock area and the Green Cape area to the south. NPWS calls the headlands hard to beat for whale watching, with southern right and humpback whales passing from September to early December. The Green Cape area has the lighthouse, campgrounds and the start of the Light to Light walk.
whyVisit: Walk the Light to Light track

goodToKnow.title: Fee only south of Eden
goodToKnow.detail: Entry is $8 per vehicle per day in areas south of Eden; the areas north of Eden are free.

goodToKnow.title: Lighthouse needs a tour
goodToKnow.detail: Green Cape Lighthouse is entered only on guided tours on set dates (10:00 AM); the grounds are open at any time.

goodToKnow.title: Light to Light takes three days
goodToKnow.detail: The 32 km walk runs from Boyds Tower to Green Cape Lighthouse with beachside campgrounds; the brief lists a $115 cost.

destination.bestTimeBlurb: {months} are the best time to see southern right and humpback whales from the headlands.
